title: How Asia Learned to Live With “America First”
gist: A paywalled teaser: the accessible text establishes only the setup — western European capitals are reeling from Trump's transactionalism and unilateralism and are either struggling to manage the risk or deferring hard choices in hope of a friendlier US president in 2028, while Japan, the Philippines, South Korea, Taiwan, and Thailand are also wary. The promised argument about how Asian allies adapted, and what Europe should learn, sits behind the paywall.

insights.claim: Western European capitals including Berlin, Madrid, and Paris are either struggling to manage the risk posed by an antagonistic US president or deferring hard adaptation choices in the hope that a friendlier successor takes office in 2028.
insights.speaker: John Lee
insights.so_what: Wait-for-2028 is an implicit bet that constrains European defense and industrial policy commitments — a reason to discount announced EU strategic-autonomy spending until after the next US election cycle.
insights.locator: In Berlin, Madrid, Paris, and other western European capitals

insights.claim: European allies' distress stems specifically from an American president who is unsentimental about decades-long alliances and uninterested in the history of transatlantic cooperation, meaning the shock is to the relationship's normative basis rather than to any single policy.
insights.speaker: John Lee
insights.so_what: Alliance risk cannot be hedged with policy concessions if the underlying commitment is transactional — expect recurring, unpredictable demands rather than a one-time renegotiation.
insights.locator: Western Europe is reeling in the face

insights.claim: Japan, the Philippines, South Korea, Taiwan, and Thailand are also wary of Trump, so Asian allies' better handling of America First reflects tactics rather than an absence of concern.
insights.speaker: John Lee
insights.so_what: Watch Asian allies' concrete accommodations — defense spending, investment pledges, tariff deals — as the template Europe will eventually be forced to copy.
insights.locator: Japan, the Philippines, South Korea, Taiwan, and Thailand
